decision: Keep offline. Continuous scores preserve the 12 hard-control editable passes and add the wolf, but worsen mean disagreement and visibly destroy details on some failed designs. Do not replace the production objective or relax acceptance gates.

findings: The oblique filled basket and reflective building have incorrect fixed crops in both arms; soft scores do not recover the intended designs. Six unresolved crops remain.
Printed ink still becomes cutting geometry on the striped/dotted G, tree/star wrapping, HO HO paper and floral paper. The confidence field contains the same confusing ink.
Both versions lose fine human/bird details in the blue/gold silhouette; both leave false channels and border defects in the flower and nested hearts.

The three-wise-men/star design is visibly worse with confidence: the star largely disappears and central silhouettes merge. Hard disagreement is 2.99625%, soft 6.149375%; missing source features increase from one to two. Neither passes the complete gates.
The octopus loses thin curled tentacles in the confidence result, increasing error from 3.135625% to 4.17875%.
The wolf improves visibly and passes both engine and independent editable paper checks. Its editable disagreement falls from 1.81875% to 1.338125%.
Several small aggregate improvements retain false seams; a passing derived-mask score is not complete recovery of the original artwork.

rootCauses.finding: Exactly zero binary-mask changes. Both timing-free ABBA replays reproduce every original coarse/fine error and finalist preference. The hard shortlist includes six cuts (phase +1); soft replaces that candidate with five cuts (phase -1). Under soft fitting, the omitted six-cut candidate still retains source regions and has 5.329895% initialization-grid disagreement, but it is not shortlisted.
rootCauses.scheduling: Hard feature-priority selection reserves grid refinement: about 2.81 s routing and 2.79 s direct refinement. Soft first-choice five-cut grid routes for about 5.44 s and leaves about 0.067 s direct refinement. This is an objective/count/routing interaction on an identical crop, not a crop or binary-classification change. The diagnostic verifies the shortlist deterministically; the later timed trajectory is one observed run.

rootCauses.finding: Both arms start with four cuts per sheet, and the ABBA initialization diagnostics replay exactly. Later routing/refinement differs. The hard final candidate has two significant floating offset-core islands totaling about 2.023 mm^2 in one sheet; confidence has none and passes the independent editable paper audit. Cut count alone does not explain the gain. This is not an isolated gradient-only causal test.

For binary renders, squared error against p equals a fixed floor plus disagreement weighted by |1-2p|. The independent audit verifies that decomposition. Confidence optimization can therefore downweight a real thin detail as well as photographic noise. Grid ranking also thresholds resampled probabilities, so identical native hard masks do not imply identical coarse objectives.

limitations: These are the same repeatedly inspected development photos, not an untouched evaluation set.
The scores use the existing training scale; calibration on real photographs has not been established.
The new hard control gives 12 passes rather than the earlier run's 11, so compare the two fresh arms, not unrelated timed baselines.
Both methods receive a ten-second search allowance; reported solve time includes final work and reaches about 10.65 seconds. Cropping/export-audit/startup time is separate.
Nominal geometry and paper checks do not establish physical assembly, tear resistance or exact original-template recovery.
nextExperiment: Hold the starting cut geometry fixed and compare binary versus continuous refinement with matched work, original mask/feature/geometry/paper gates, and all failed cases retained. This separates useful boundary forces from changing count selection and routing budgets.
